subject: StNew Clinic RFP: PHI handling assessment and BAA next steps
messages:
From: Emily Sanders <emily.sanders@stnewclinic.org>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@stnewclinic.org
Date: Mon, 4 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: RFP: PHI handling assessment + BAA requirements

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking our RFP. Attached is Section C of our procurement packet focused on PHI/data protection (StNew_Healthcare_RFP_SectionC.pdf). We need: a completed capability questionnaire, a statement of deployment options for PHI (hosted vs dedicated vs private), and an initial BAA redline if you have one.

Key timeline: procurement board meets next Thursday (2027-05-13). Could you return the questionnaire and any redlines by COB next Wednesday (2027-05-12)? Also please flag anything that would require additional legal review or third-party evidence (SOC 2, penetration test, KMS attestations, etc.).

Quick clarifying items:
- We will need details on where PHI may be cached (KV cache, logs) and retention defaults.
- We require customer-managed keys or private deployment for production PHI workloads; any hosted options must support Bring Your Own Key.
- Token-level cost/latency reporting and audit logs for requests touching PHI are mandatory for our compliance group.

Emily Sanders
Senior Procurement Manager
StNew Clinic

Attachments: StNew_Healthcare_RFP_SectionC.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Sanders <emily.sanders@stnewclinic.org>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: PHI handling assessment + BAA requirements

Emily — thanks, received. We're happy to support StNew on this. Please find an initial draft of our questionnaire responses attached (Redwood_PHIAssess_Draft.xlsx). High level:

- Deployment options: Hosted (with BYOK/KMS integrations for advanced tiers), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools with isolated tenancy), Private (VPC or on-prem appliance for fully customer-controlled networking). We can map the workload to any of these models during onboarding.
- PHI in transit: TLS 1.2+; mutual TLS available for private instances.
- Encryption at rest: AES-256 for hosted/dedicated; customer-managed keys (Cloud KMS / HSM) supported for Dedicated/Private and available for Hosted via BYOK contract.
- Caching & KV: Runtime uses ephemeral KV caches per inference session. For PHI workloads we recommend disabling prefix caching on Hosted and enabling explicit KV lifecycle controls on Dedicated/Private.
- Auditing: Token-level request tracing, per-request cost/latency metrics, and full access logs are available and can be retained per your retention policy.

I'll coordinate legal redlines with our counsel (cc'd Laura). Can we schedule a 30-min call tomorrow or Wednesday to walk through any high-risk items?

Next steps suggested:
1) Review the attached draft questionnaire and mark any items you want deeper evidence for.
2) Quick technical call to confirm KV/cache behavior and BYOK workflows.
3) Legal to exchange redline BAA v0.1.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
karthik@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: Redwood_PHIAssess_Draft.xlsx (xlsx, 48KB)
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Sanders <emily.sanders@stnewclinic.org>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2027 09:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: PHI handling assessment + BAA requirements

Emily — Laura from Legal here. Thanks for the packet. We've prepared an initial redline for your BAA (attached: redlined_baa_v0.1.pdf). High-level flags we expect you to consider:

- Subprocessors: we list our core infra providers and will accept a data export/notice mechanism for adding new subprocessors, plus a 30-day review period for enterprise contracts.
- Data retention & deletion: propose a standard retention model with options for shorter retention on Dedicated/Private. Will need to agree SLA for deletion and attestations.
- Audits & evidence: SOC 2 Type II report is available under NDA; we can provide penetration test summaries and a redacted vulnerability tracker for enterprise customers.
- KMS/Key control: BYOK for Hosted requires a contractual key escrow exception; fully private deployments avoid the escrow requirement.
- Liability/indemnity: propose mutual indemnities limited to direct damages and carve-outs for gross negligence.

Please see the redline for suggested language. If these items look acceptable, we can prepare a clean BAA to progress to DocuSign after your internal review. Happy to join a call with your legal/compliance team.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal and Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redlined_baa_v0.1.pdf (pdf, 92KB)
From: Emily Sanders <emily.sanders@stnewclinic.org>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@stnewclinic.org
Date: Wed, 6 May 2027 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: PHI handling assessment + BAA requirements

Thanks Karthik and Laura — that's helpful. A few quick clarifications from our security and compliance teams before we move to redline acceptance:

1) Token-level logs: are request logs stored with full input payloads by default? We need to understand what is logged and whether we can disable full payload retention for PHI workloads.
2) KV cache residency: for Dedicated instances, confirm whether KV cache can be pinned to the same tenant storage and whether it is encrypted with customer keys.
3) Key rotation: what is your recommended rotation window for customer-managed keys and do you support automated key rotation without downtime?
4) Evidence access: provide the link for SOC 2 and pen test summaries under NDA and confirm who at Redwood will be our point of contact for audit requests.

Also, procurement asked if we can get an initial DocuSign timeline. We are aiming to close vendor selection by 2027-05-13 if all evidence looks good.

Emily Sanders
Senior Procurement Manager
StNew Clinic
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Sanders <emily.sanders@stnewclinic.org>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 6 May 2027 15:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: PHI handling assessment + BAA requirements

Emily — quick answers so you can brief your teams: short version below, happy to expand on the technical call.

1) Logs: By default we record request metadata and truncated inputs for observability. For PHI workloads we can disable payload retention and enable token-level traces that do not persist full input payloads. We will include a configuration matrix in the technical call.
2) KV cache: On Dedicated and Private the KV cache can be configured to use tenant-isolated storage and encrypted with customer-managed keys. Hosted BYOK also supports encrypted caches but requires a higher tier and contractual BYOK setup.
3) Key rotation: We recommend a 90-day rotation window; for BYOK/HSM customers we support automated rotation with zero-downtime key rollover (key versions and wrap/unwrap flows).
4) Evidence: SOC 2 Type II and pen-test summaries are available under NDA — link: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-evidence-link (password has been shared via our portal). Point of contact for audits: Marissa Cole (marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com).

DocuSign: if legal confirms the redline, we can issue a DocuSign within 48 hours. DocuSign placeholder: https://app.docusign.com/transaction/ABC123

Proposed next steps: 1) Tech call tomorrow 10:00 AM PT (we'll invite Zoom), 2) Legal to finalize redline after your feedback, 3) Issue DocuSign if redline accepted.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
